sentences.text: Justice
Arvind Singh Chandel Order On Board Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:18260 20/07/2023 1.

This appeal has been preferred by the appellants under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 21.11.2014 passed by the Third Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Ambikapur, District Surguja (C.G.) in Motor Accidents Claims Case No.121/2012, whereby the learned Tribunal has passed the award of compensation amount of Rs.4,99,000/- in favour of the respondents herein and fastened the liability for payment for compensation amount to the appellants herein, i.e., owner and driver of the offending vehicle.

entities.text: Third Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Ambikapur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Hence, this appeal.

2. The Respondents/Claimants No.1 to 4 are legal heirs of deceased Inder Ram preferred the claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act inter alia on the ground that on 29.03.2009,
deceased Inder Ram went along with his associates Rameshwar, Devraj and others from Jashpur to Kusmi by traveling by bus bearing registration number C.G. 15 ZA 0156 (offending vehilce).

At the time when the deceased trying to enter into the bus, the Conductor of the bus without seeing Inder Ram while entering into the bus asked the Driver to go ahead and on the advice given by the Conductor, the Driver started the bus in a rash and negligent manner and as a result of which, the deceased Inder Ram came under the wheels of the bus/offending vehicle and died.

At the time of accident, the deceased was working as a Mason (Rajmistri) and Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:18260 also doing the work of agriculture and was earning monthly salary of Rs.4,000/-.
3.
In the claim petition, the Claimants claimed compensation amount of Rs.34,01,000/- under various heads.

In their written statements, appellants herein denying the averments made by the Claimants and stated that the deceased was a mentally retarded person and also at the time of accident, the deceased was in a drunken condition and the deceased was himself responsible for the said accident, therefore, the appellants are not entitled to pay any compensation to the Claimants.

4. After examining the witnesses and after considering the evidence available on record, the learned Tribunal vide award dated 21.11.2014 passed and award of Rs.4,99,000/- fixing liability upon the appellants.
Hence, this appeal.
5. Learned counsel appearing for the appellants would submit that though the trial Court in criminal case convicted the Driver and the Conductor of the offending vehicle.

However, the appellate Court vide its judgment dated 07.08.2012 acquitted both the Driver and the Conductor holding that on the date of accident the deceased was in drunken condition and his mental condition was also not found fit.

He also submits that from the admission made by eye witness of the case, i.e., applicant witness No.3-Sahdev who is real brother of the deceased Inder Ram, it is also established that at the time of Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:18260 accident, the deceased was trying to enter in the running bus due to that incident occurred, therefore, there was a clear cut contributory negligence available on the part of the deceased.
Thus, the appellants would be liable to pay only 50% compensation amount of their part.
6. After services of notice, no one appears on behalf of the respondents.

sentences.text: I have heard learned counsel appearing for the appellants and perused the entire evidence adduced by the parties before the Claim Tribunal minutely.

8. Before the Tribunal, the Claimants were examined as many as three witnesses out of them,
witness No.3-Sahdev was the eye witness and as per his statement at the time of accident also, he was with the deceased.

In his Court statements paragraph-4, he categorically admitted the fact that on the date of accident as per their customs, he along with the deceased and other companion were taken liquor and thereafter they reached Lavkushpur for getting bus.
He further admitted that when the bus was started and run then the deceased was attempt to enter in the bus.

9. From the above mentioned admission made by this witness, it is established that at the time of accident, when the offending vehicle was run then the deceased was attempt to enter into the bus due to Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:18260 that accident occurred, therefore, it is clear that there is contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.
10.

As held by this Court there was a contributory negligence on the part of the deceased, therefore,
the appellants are liable to pay 50% of amount of the award as ordered by the Tribunal.
11. Accordingly, the instant appeal is allowed in part.
